symptom: `mxcli exec probe.mdl --mcp <url> --mcp-trace` (and `-c`, the REPL, `mcp capabilities`) printed `▸ connect local …` and `▸ CreateConstantStmt` but no PED tool call, so a reporter concluded the write went to the .mpr on disk instead of Studio Pro (mendixlabs/mxcli#1684). A fake Studio Pro received ped_get_schema, ped_create_document and six ped_check_errors in the same run
cause: Tracing has two halves: the executor prints statements (Executor.SetTracer, wired in newLoggedExecutorTo) and the MCP client prints calls from Backend.tracer, set only by mcpbackend.WithTracer. newBackendFactory and the mcp capabilities command built the backend with mcpbackend.New alone; WithTracer had no caller outside tests, although executor.go's SetTracer comment says the backend must get it too
fix: Build the MCP backend with .WithTracer(mcpTracer()) in both places
insight: A diagnostic flag that prints half its output is worse than none: the missing half reads as a negative result. When a report's evidence is a trace or a log line that is absent, check that the thing producing that line is wired before believing the absence; a logging fake server on the other end settled it in one run. The test drives the CLI's own executor builder against a fake PED and compares the trace with what the fake received
